items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Eddie Safranski and I were the two hot guys, and they would add us to the other six who were playing with the NBC Orchestra.

ctx.x: Well I did jazz playing, not so much with him, no. He had a feel for it. You know he was with the Philharmonic and he taught at Juilliard during that period. He wasn’t a jazz player but he was loose. He was a good golfer, he was a marvelous painter, and he loved the bass, he adored the bass. And he was just — I studied privately and he taught at Juilliard but I just studied privately with him. And as time went on he was very kind to me and I used to come in evenings and he’d play duets with me and things like…
Symphony and as well as the dance orchestra. Eddie Safranski and I were the two hot guys, and they would add us to the other six who were playing with the NBC Orchestra.
Is that the term they used, the “hot guys?”
